maya: Quick heads-up — ran a large perf sweep on continuous-batching heuristics this morning, focusing on max-batch-size and max-tokens-per-batch per GPU (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). Found a surprising regress on L4 after the new kernel-selector change. :eyes:

lucas: ugh — which regression? latency, tail p99, or throughput?

maya: tail p99 for short-chat workloads (avg seq len ~32) jumped ~18% on the L4 pool. throughput didn't tank but latency variance is worse.

lucas: that aligns with a kernel fallback I landed yesterday — fallback picks a different matmul kernel for small seqs if KV fragmentation > 0.6. Could be choosing a slower path for short sequences.

maya: exact numbers from the profiling run:
```
GPU  workload  p50(ms)  p95(ms)  p99(ms)  toks/batch
A10  short     12       28       45       8192
T4   short     18       42       68       6144
L4   short     11       36       53       4096  <-- p99 spike
A100 short     9        22       35       32768
H100 short     8        20       33       65536
```

priya: interesting — L4 has lower max tokens/batch in the trace (4096) vs A10 (8192). Did the sweep change the per-device max_tokens_per_batch policy?

lucas: yes, I tightened `max_tokens_per_batch` for L4 to avoid OOMs when many concurrent streams hit the KV cache. The new kernel route seems sensitive to the lower token packing and ends up breaking the fast small-kernel.

anton: I also saw KV cache fragmentation higher on L4; due to smaller per-GPU packing the cache ends up with more fragmented entries which bumps the kernel-selector score. Suggested fix: add a short-path that ignores fragmentation for seq_len <= 64.

maya: that could work. Alternatively we can adjust `max_batch_size` and `max_tokens_per_batch` per GPU in the routing policy to give L4 slightly larger token budgets for short-chat workloads. Proposed quick table:
```
proposal_v1:
A10: max_batch_size=64, max_tokens_per_batch=8192
T4:  max_batch_size=48, max_tokens_per_batch=6144
L4:  max_batch_size=48, max_tokens_per_batch=8192  # bump
A100: max_batch_size=128, max_tokens_per_batch=32768
H100: max_batch_size=256, max_tokens_per_batch=65536
```

priya: bumping L4 token budget makes sense for chat-first tenants. Need to be careful about multi-tenant bursts — set a per-tenant cap so a single tenant can't consume the whole device.

lucas: agreed. Also we should update the kernel-selector's feature set to include `seq_len_bucket` so it can prefer small-seq optimized kernels regardless of KV fragmentation.

sasha: I'll run an experiment matrix across (max_tokens_per_batch = [4096, 6144, 8192]) × (max_batch_size = [32,48,64]) on L4 and T4 pools, capture p50/p95/p99 and KV fragmentation metric. Will post results in this thread. ETA ~3h.

opsbot: Deploy started: kernel-selector v2.8 -> canary -> eng-runtime-l4 (triggered by lucas). Build: bld-2026.03.18-2310

maya: thanks. For the experiment, include synthetic short-chat (seq 16–48), mixed (16–512), and long (512–2048) profiles. We need to ensure we don't regress long-tail large-seq workloads when increasing token caps.

anton: note — when we increase max_tokens_per_batch we may cause more KV fragments per allocation; include KV eviction pressure in telemetry. If eviction rate > 0.02 then abort the config.

lucas: good guardrail. I'll also add a quick circuit-breaker in the runtime: if p99 increases >15% for any workload after rollout, automatically revert canary.

sasha: quick status update — first batch of runs done on L4:
- 4096/48: baseline, p99=52ms, kv_frag=0.63
- 6144/48: p99=47ms, kv_frag=0.68
- 8192/48: p99=36ms, kv_frag=0.76 (best latency but higher fragmentation)

priya: fragmentation 0.76 is high but if eviction stays low maybe acceptable for chat tiers. What's eviction rate?

sasha: eviction rates: 0.004, 0.008, 0.021 respectively. 8192 case crosses the 0.02 threshold.

maya: so 8192 gives best latency but risks eviction-induced work. 6144 seems like a good middle ground.

lucas: I'll prototype kernel-selector tweak to prefer small-seq kernel when seq_len <= 64. If that reduces p99 at 4096 config we might avoid bumping tokens.

anton: also propose a KV-aware packing improvement: prefer coalescing requests with similar KV key prefixes to reduce fragmentation. That change is moderate risk but could lower frag without increasing token caps.

maya: action items:
- sasha: finish matrix for T4 and validate eviction telemetry (ETA 3h)
- lucas: add seq_len_bucket feature to kernel-selector and run microbenchmarks (ETA EOD)
- anton: prototype prefix-coalescing for packing (low-priority experiment)
- priya: draft routing policy update for L4 chat-optimized tenants with per-tenant caps

priya: noted. I'll draft the routing PL and include gating via eviction metric and p99 canary checks.

maya: cool — thanks team. We'll reconvene once Sasha posts T4 results. :thumbsup:
